source.title: MotifAE Reveals Functional Sequence Patterns from Protein Language Model: Unsupervised Discovery and Interpretability Analysis
source.authors: Chao Hou; Di Liu; Yu-Feng Shen

record.file_problem: The text is a full article in press, not an abstract or garbled extract. Its title and DOI differ from the supplied metadata: the text is titled “Unsupervised discovery of functional sequence patterns from protein language model with MotifAE” and gives DOI 10.1038/s41467-026-77333-2.
record.tranche_reason: Applies sparse-autoencoder feature discovery to ESM2 protein-language-model representations, a new model setting, and reports results on recovered motif and domain patterns. It does not test the original toy-network superposition mechanism.
record.gate_note: The study measures whether SAE/MotifAE features align with annotated motifs, domains, and residue-function measurements. Reported comparisons and feature-to-annotation results are included. The feature-count and matching analyses describe recovered patterns, not evidence that capacity pressure caused polysemanticity. Fitness-prediction and protein-redesign results that do not measure feature recovery or canonicality are omitted.
record.test_reason: The paper builds MotifAE, an SAE variant with a smoothness loss, on ESM2-650M embeddings. It reports how well that method and a standard SAE match motifs, domains and DMS residue importance. It assumes the SAE premise (embeddings are linear combinations of features) and does not test superposition. There is no raw-neuron or embedding baseline (the authors omit it, citing prior work), no capacity, sparsity or geometry analysis, and no stability or canonicality test across dictionaries. Its results are its own method's performance against a standard SAE.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also report that features with similar decoder weights give similar PSSMs. They add that a supervised gate (MotifAE-G) selects stability-associated features that improve stability prediction and steer in-silico redesign. They do not frame any result as evidence about superposition.
record.recipe_differences: This is not a reproduction of the toy-network method. It trains SAE and smoothness-regularized MotifAE dictionaries on ESM2-650M protein embeddings and evaluates alignment to biological annotations and experiments; it does not test toy-network superposition geometry or sparsity transitions.
record.method_sensitivity: The smoothness window size was tested at three, four, and five residues; the authors report similar performance. Results also vary with region type and domain contact order.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE and MotifAE features trained on ESM2-650M last-layer embeddings align with annotated ELM motifs (median best-match AUROC 0.80 for SAE, 0.88 for MotifAE). They also align with CATH domains and correlate with DMS residue importance. The smoothness loss improves alignment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse dictionary features from protein language models align with biologically annotated sequence patterns, and biologically informed priors (smoothness) improve that alignment.

fits_no_version.finding: Feature–annotation matches are many-to-many. 67 of 114 matched motifs are matched by multiple features, and 55 of 146 features match multiple motifs, e.g. f27416 matches 17 C-terminal motifs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dictionary features in pLMs vary in granularity relative to human annotation categories.

record.problems: No stability across independently trained dictionaries or completeness of the feature set is established. The article says shuffled-weight SAE controls were omitted based on prior work. Domain identification is weaker for high-contact-order domains, and the “others” CATH class comparison is nonsignificant with n = 8.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. Results for protein fitness prediction and MotifAE-G stability-guided redesign were left out because they evaluate reconstructed-embedding fitness or an induced redesign objective, not feature recovery or canonicality.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity sweep, phase transition or geometry.
No test of capacity competition or dedicated dimensions for important features.
No alternative causes of polysemanticity examined.
No neuron-level polysemanticity or distributed-feature measurement. No raw-embedding or shuffled-weight baseline, so SAE recovery is not shown to reflect superposition.
No stability across seeds or dictionary sizes, completeness or canonicality analysis. Only annotation-matching granularity is reported.
No comparison of 1-D versus multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: The text's title and DOI differ from the metadata; the text is the Nature Communications version of the bioRxiv preprint. This is primarily a protein-interpretability methods paper. Using the SAE architecture presupposes the dictionary/superposition framing but does not test it. The authors explicitly omitted raw-embedding and shuffled-weight controls, so no row can bear on V4. No verdict labels are given.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, feature-sparsity sweep, superposition geometry, or sparsity-dependent transition is tested.
The study does not test whether features compete for limited dimensions, whether important features receive dedicated dimensions, or whether that mechanism causes neuron polysemanticity.
No alternative cause of polysemantic neurons is tested.
The tested setting is ESM2-650M protein embeddings, not other LLMs or language-model families; the study does not measure neuron-level feature spreading directly.
The study examines feature-to-motif and feature-to-domain matching and reports varying granularity. It does not establish feature completeness, stability across training runs, or canonicality.
No comparison of one-dimensional feature directions against multidimensional features is made.

rows.subject: MotifAE
rows.size_stated: 40,960 latent dimensions; trained on ESM2-650M embeddings (1280 dimensions)
rows.operation_detail: Used each latent feature activation score to identify residues in annotated ELM motifs; reported median AUROC of the best-matching feature.

conditions.value: 270 ELM motifs with at least 20 residues in verified regions

rows.locator: Results, “MotifAE captures known functional motifs”; Fig. 3A, C
rows.note: Authors report MotifAE significantly outperformed the standard SAE.
rows.check: Compares the study's own method with a standard SAE on annotation alignment. With no neuron or embedding baseline it cannot show that features are spread or superposed.

rows.subject: MotifAE
rows.size_stated: 40,960 latent dimensions; trained on ESM2-650M embeddings (1280 dimensions)
rows.operation_detail: Counted motif-feature matches, defining a match as AUROC > 0.9.
rows.measure: Number and distribution of matched motif-feature pairs
rows.value: 322 matched pairs involving 114 ELM motifs and 146 MotifAE features; 47 motifs matched by one feature and 67 by multiple features; 91 features matched one motif and 55 multiple motifs
rows.locator: Results, “MotifAE captures known functional motifs”; Fig. 3D–E
rows.note: The many-to-many matching and varying granularity qualify a one-feature/one-motif account.
rows.check: Many-to-many motif–feature matches reflect annotation granularity. They do not test completeness, stability or canonicality of features as model units, so the V5 link is unwarranted.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: ESM2-650M protein-language-model embeddings; ELM motif and CATH domain annotations; ProteinGYM residue-importance measurements
reader_labels.reason: SAE-family feature activations identify annotated motifs and domains and correlate with residue importance; MotifAE reports AUROC and correlation results across these evaluations (R1–R7, R11–R19).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: CATH domain identification, especially domains with high contact order and the small “others” class
reader_labels.reason: Performance declines for high-contact-order domains; the comparison in the “others” class is not significant and has no textual AUROC values (R20–R21).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: ELM motif and CATH domain feature matching
reader_labels.reason: The reported mappings are many-to-many and include features that match multiple motifs or domains, so the results do not support treating every SAE feature as a one-to-one canonical unit (R8–R10, R13).
